finding: The F-AHL15 derivative-consistent, floor-scaled shared-support representation preserves the frozen Richards fidelity gates and yields a paired complete-solve CPU reduction in every tested material-regime combination.
research_claim: Within the tested four-material, wet-mid-dry prescribed-head-bottom Richards matrix, auto-generated derivative-consistent hydraulic lookup reduces complete Richards solve CPU by approximately 21-27% while preserving the analytical nonlinear iteration/backtracking path and the preregistered response gates.
limits: The matrix uses four selected unimodal materials and prescribed-head lower boundaries.
This is a Richards-solver result, not yet a whole-SWAP application runtime result.
Build cost, cache reuse and many-column amortization are not yet included.
Other hydraulic model families and SWKIMPL=1/dKdh are outside current authority.
Surface-boundary redesign and groundwater-coupling tangent behavior remain separate future questions.
next_phase: Engineering qualification of auto-generation, fingerprinted immutable caching, build-cost amortization and production-runtime integration without changing hydraulic science.
